meta.title: LanguageTool — Batch localize for Mac
meta.description: A macOS localization utility for iOS, Flutter, and Electron. Convert, review, and ship multilingual releases faster.

home.headline: Ship multilingual releases without the spreadsheet grind.
home.support: Batch-localize iOS, Flutter, and Electron files—then review before you export.
home.cta: Download on the Mac App Store
home.cap1Body: Pick a platform, choose target languages, and generate localization files in one pass.
home.cap2Body: Inspect keys, spot missing strings, and polish translations before they land in your repo.
home.cap3Body: Native support for .strings / .xcstrings, Flutter .arb, and Electron .json.
home.closeTitle: Ready when your next locale is.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.lead: Get LanguageTool running and through your first localization pass.
docs.reqBody: macOS 13.0 or later. For iOS string catalogs, Xcode 15+ is recommended on the machine that consumes the output.
docs.getBody: Install LanguageTool from the Mac App Store. Launch once, then open Settings if you want to connect your own translation service endpoint.
docs.step1: Choose a platform: iOS, Flutter, or Electron.
docs.step2: Select the source file and output location, then pick target languages.
docs.step3: Start conversion. Open Review to check results, export CSV, or sync back.
docs.faq1Q: Can I skip strings that already have translations?
docs.faq1A: Yes. Enable “Skip existing translations” so only missing keys are generated.
docs.faq2A: Review is a table of keys and locales so you can verify, filter missing rows, and export before shipping.
docs.faq3A: iOS .strings / .xcstrings, Flutter .arb, and Electron localized .json files.
docs.faq4Q: Do I need an API key?
docs.faq4A: Only if you want AI-assisted translation via your own provider account. The key authenticates your account; it is not sold by LanguageTool.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: LanguageTool is designed to keep your localization work on your Mac.
privacy.s1Body: The Mac app does not require an LanguageTool account. Localization files you open stay under your control on your device unless you explicitly send them to a third-party service you configure.
privacy.s2Body: If you enter an API key for a third-party AI or translation provider, requests go to that provider under your account. LanguageTool does not sell API keys and does not operate those services.
privacy.s3Body: Purchases and downloads through the Mac App Store are handled by Apple under Apple’s privacy policy.
privacy.s4Body: For privacy questions about this app, use the support contact listed on the Mac App Store product page.
